Demo recap (high level):

- Traffic shape: expected bursts during batch settlement windows and sustained 200–300 qps during peak daytime.
- Streaming: client requires token-by-token streaming for progressive UI updates (important for UX).

Performance targets you called out:

- Sustained throughput: 200–300 qps (peaks to ~500 qps for short bursts)
- Concurrency: ~150–250 concurrent streaming sessions
- Availability goal: 99.9% SLA for production workloads

Attached is an SLO checklist (slo_checklist.xlsx) we fill out jointly. The checklist has specific measurement definitions so we all count the same thing (p95 measured from request received by gateway to first token out + network disclaimers). Also attaching perf_capture_instructions.txt for your infra team — this outlines a short 30-minute capture we request to reproduce traffic shape and validate p95 and concurrency.

Thanks Dana — happy to clarify. Short answers up front: server-side gateway measurement is what we recommend for contractual SLOs, and yes, token streaming at the cadence you described is achievable with the right config (minimal batching for latency-sensitive streams). Details below.

Measurement definition:
- We recommend measuring p95 at the Redwood gateway (time request received at gateway -> time first token emitted by our runtime). This excludes client network variability and TLS handshake time, which keeps SLOs actionable. We're calling that "p95 server-first-token" in the checklist.

Streaming behavior and batching:
- Default: our runtime does continuous batching to maximize throughput. For latency-sensitive streams you can:
  - Use a low-latency profile (no/minimal batching, aggressive kernel choices) — best for p95 first-token.
  - Use a mixed profile: small batching (e.g., 8–16ms windows) to balance throughput/cost and keep first-token under ~200ms in most cases.
- Subsequent-token cadence: once the model starts streaming, subsequent tokens are typically sub-30–60ms depending on model size and decoding settings. For sub-50ms steady intervals on a heavy model we recommend a Dedicated pool with larger memory GPUs.

Concurrency vs QPS:
- Concurrency = number of simultaneous open streaming connections. QPS = number of new requests per second. They interact because higher concurrency means the runtime needs more parallel KV cache state and memory but fewer reasons to batch aggressively. For your numbers (~200–250 concurrent streams + 200–300 qps sustained) a Dedicated pool with autoscaling headroom for 2x burst (up to ~500 qps) is the recommended config.

Recommended perf capture config (we'll run this on a Dedicated-like node):
- 30-minute capture using your synthetic workload (attached).
- Two profiles: low-latency (minimal batching) and balanced (small batching) — we capture p50/p95/p99 server-first-token, tail CPU/GPU metrics, and contention metrics.
- We'll return a short artifact (perf_results_30min_capture.tar.gz) with raw traces and a summary report.

I'll own running the capture and returning results. Can Marissa confirm the Tue 2/24 window and that we have the synthetic workload file from FintechCo?

— Aditya
